**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/18 (Thu) 00:26
- [FACT] User inquired about the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) and its role in nuclear energy safety.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The IAEA promotes and ensures the safe use of nuclear energy worldwide through various activities.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The IAEA develops international safety standards for nuclear facilities, radiation protection, and disposal of nuclear waste.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The IAEA conducts safety reviews of nuclear power plants, research reactors, and other nuclear facilities.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The IAEA provides technical assistance to member states to enhance their nuclear safety infrastructure.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The IAEA assists member states in developing emergency preparedness and response plans for nuclear incidents.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The IAEA monitors radiation levels at nuclear facilities and in the environment.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The IAEA promotes efforts to enhance nuclear security and prevent unauthorized use of nuclear material.
- [USER] Asked for recent examples of IAEA interventions to ensure safe nuclear energy use in member states.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The IAEA intervened in Iran in 2015 to monitor compliance with a nuclear agreement.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The IAEA assisted Japan after the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster in 2011.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The IAEA has worked with Ukraine to improve safety and security of its nuclear facilities since the Chernobyl disaster.
- [USER] Inquired about how the IAEA ensures compliance with safety standards and consequences for non-compliance.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The IAEA uses safeguards to verify that nuclear material is used for peaceful purposes.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The IAEA conducts regular inspections of nuclear facilities for compliance with safety standards.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Member states must submit regular reports to the IAEA on their nuclear activities and safety measures.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Consequences for non-compliance include reporting to the UN Security Council, denying technical assistance, and recommending sanctions.
- [USER] Asked if member states could hide non-compliance from the IAEA and how the organization prevents this.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] It is possible for member states to hide non-compliance, but the IAEA employs various inspection techniques to prevent this.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The IAEA uses remote monitoring, unannounced inspections, and environmental sampling.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Member states are required to report regularly to the IAEA on their nuclear activities.
- [USER] Asked about the IAEA's authority over member states regarding nuclear energy regulation
